subject: Secure Edge Install Readiness — Medix Health RFI
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Offline/air-gapped install readiness and operational controls

Mina / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — it was helpful. As we move toward procurement for the Medix edge initiative, our security team has a short list of clarifications we need for on-prem/offline deployments. Can you confirm the following at a high level so we can include it in our RFP response packet?

- Do you support fully air-gapped installations (no outbound connections) for inference runtime and control plane? If partial, what controls are required?
- How are patches and security updates delivered in an offline environment? Do you provide an SBOM and signed manifests?
- What operational runbooks / playbooks do you provide for offline incident response (e.g., key compromise, kernel updates, emergency rollback)?
- Network architecture: do you provide recommended diagrams for segregated edge clusters and firewalled management networks?

We have a tight deadline — procurement wants the RFI evidence pack by Feb 15. If you can share a checklist and any sample artefacts (network diagram, SBOM, deployment playbook), that would be ideal.

Oliver
Procurement Lead, Medix Health
oliver.grant@medixhealth.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Offline/air-gapped install readiness and operational controls

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a concise deliverable set tailored for procurement: an operational readiness checklist, a recommended network diagram (v2), and our SBOM manifest with signed hashes. High-level answers below; the checklist goes into the procedural details you asked for.

- Air-gapped installs: Supported. We provide a standalone control plane image and an inference runtime package that can be installed without outbound connectivity. Admin tooling (optional) can run from an isolated management workstation. Offline install requires initial package transfer via secure media (USB/NDEx) and an on-site signing verification step we document in the checklist.

- Patching & updates: We produce signed patch bundles and a SHA256 manifest. For air-gapped sites, standard cadence is quarterly security bundles plus emergency hotfixes. We provide instructions for validating signatures and for applying delta patches to minimize downtime. The attached sha256-sbom-manifest.txt is an example bundle index.

- Incident runbooks: We include playbooks for kernel/OS patching coordination, KMS key rotation (customer-managed KMS recommended), and rollback procedures for model artifacts and runtime images. Runbooks include verification steps, expected timelines, and escalation contact templates.

- Network architecture: See network-diagram-v2.png for a two-tier segmented layout: isolated inference cluster, a management bastion in a fenced management VLAN, and an optional ephemeral jump host for signed media ingestion. We note firewall rules, required ports (none egress by default), and recommended IDS placement.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-offline-deploy-checklist.pdf (PDF, 82KB)], [Attachment: network-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 180KB)], [Attachment: sha256-sbom-manifest.txt (TXT, 12KB)].

Next steps: If you want, Marissa can set up a 30-min run-through with your security team to validate the checklist and answer technical questions.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Liu <rachel.liu@securitas.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2028 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Re: RFI: Offline/air-gapped install readiness and operational controls

Forwarding the checklist and diagram — a couple of quick clarifications from Medix's note:

- Rachel: can you confirm whether Medix will require us to use their on-prem KMS or if a customer-managed HSM (with connectors) is acceptable? The runbook assumes customer KMS integration; we have an HSM connector and documented key rotation steps but want to ensure it meets their auditors.

- Oliver: on the network diagram, notice the optional ephemeral jump host we recommended. In practice, many of our customers use a physically isolated media transfer station (locked room) plus signed manifests to meet audit controls. If you need, we can add a short addendum showing the media transfer SOP.

For Securitas: attaching a short hardened config excerpt that shows the minimal firewall policy we recommend for air-gapped clusters (snippet included in redwood-offline-deploy-checklist.pdf).

[Attachment: hardened-firewall-snippet.txt (TXT, 4KB)]

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Offline/air-gapped install readiness and operational controls

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the artifacts. These look suitable for our RFI packet. A couple of quick items before we close:

1) Can you provide a one-page attestation statement we can include in the evidence appendix stating the offline install process and SBOM signing practice (we can add it to the RFP bundle)?
2) Procurement prefers documents signed or routed via DocuSign if possible. Can you send the attestation and the standard offline ops SOW for signature?

If you can get those in by Feb 16, we should be on track. Otherwise, we'll flag the item but it may slow procurement.

Appreciate it — Oliver
